ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Satishchandra.R, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.Ashok.N.Patil, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
2. The claimant is before this Court challenging the order that is rendered by the Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in MVC No.3384/2020 dated NC: 2024:KHC:37163 01.08.2022.

sentences.text:
When the appellant projected a claim for Rs.15,00,000/- as compensation, the Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.1,23,700/- as compensation divided under following heads:

6 Loss of amenities Rs.50,000  Total Rs.1,23,700

3. Arguing the matter, Sri.Satishchandra.R,
learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant sustained grievous injuries due to the accident.
The appellant was working as delivery boy at Zomato by the date of accident.
However, due to the injury sustained he lost his earnings.
Though through the evidence of Pw.3, NC: 2024:KHC:37163 the aspect of disability was established, the Tribunal did not award any amount under the head loss of future earnings which is unjustifiable.

Learned counsel also contends that the sum awarded as compensation under all other heads is also grossly low and therefore, the appeal is filed.
4.

Sri.Ashok.N.Patil, on the other hand states that the Tribunal, taking into consideration the totality of the facts, awarded a justifiable sum as compensation and therefore, the award needs no interference.
5. It is not in dispute that the appellant sustained fracture of 4th and 5th metatarsal bones and underwent debridement and K wires fixation.
It is brought on record that the appellant took treatment as inpatient for two days.
Pw.3 spoke about the alleged disability basing on the complaint of the appellant.
Apart from that there is no substantive proof to show that there is permanent physical disability.

However, considering the fact that the appellant sustained fracture of metatarsal bones and underwent NC: 2024:KHC:37163 surgery, this Court is of the view that the appellant would not have attended his normal pursuits at least for a period of two months.
Also the sum awarded under the head pain and suffering requires slight enhancement.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that globally the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- in addition to the sum that is awarded by the Tribunal.

6. Thus the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation that is awarded by the Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru through orders in MVC No.3384/2020 dated 01.08.2022 is enhanced by Rs.30,000/-.
